findings.obligation: One owner per decided fact, reuse before create: nw-code-craftsmanship rule 2 and rule 10, and nw-code-design-oo rule 2 - a second unit answering a question an existing owner in the same file already answers is a defect even when the code differs.
findings.observation: The new helper fn attribute(markup, needle) -> Option<String> reads an attribute value by searching for the literal needle href=" and taking the text up to the next double quote. xtask/src/check_arch.rs:2048 already owns that question: fn tag_attribute(tag, name) -> Option<String> resolves name="..." or name='...', and unlike the new one it checks that the match starts at an attribute boundary and accepts either quote style, so the new helper is a strictly weaker duplicate (it would also match a needle inside another attribute's value). Its only caller is member_name at :2253, the refusal text's fallback name for a member that has no word, so the defect is a maintenance one rather than a wrong verdict: the layer's pass or fail outcome does not depend on it. RPP level 2 duplication in a changed unit; severity medium, non-blocking.
findings.remediation: Delete fn attribute and call the existing owner from member_name: tag_attribute(member, "href") returns the same value for every lawfully authored member and keeps one owner of attribute reading in this file.

Scope and authority check. The Request has two halves; the second, making the left nav collapsible, is recorded in the authority brief's own Scope as already delivered by nav-collapse-toggle and nav-collapse-icon-rail in v0.19.0 (docs/feature/nav-quick-actions/brief.md Scope, and the released CHANGELOG v0.19.0 entry describes both), with a dated confirmed user decision for each of the three owner choices this candidate implements: remove Home's Quick actions once the links are in the nav, place the three after Board, and change no rights. That is a human-authorised scope statement with provenance, not a producer-side reduction, and the oracle still carries the collapsed-rail obligation for the three new members as P4 rather than dropping it. Design-quality reading against the bound paradigm (procedural, so the universal craftsmanship rules only): no fact is decided twice in production - templates/partials/sidebar.html stays the single member list, NavContext stays the single carrier of the three rights facts on the page, and the three destinations are literal hrefs with no new carrier; every refusal the candidate adds, in the check-arch layer and in the new step module, states WHAT failed, WHY it matters and HOW to fix it with the offending member named; no untrusted input, path, command, secret or persisted datum is involved (no route, handler, query or authorization is touched); no performance claim is made. Two residues are design decisions recorded with their cost rather than defects: the unreferenced .actions rules stay in the content-hash-named stylesheet to avoid re-fingerprinting it and migrating three cache-policy assertions, and the icon shape-child provenance for users, user-plus and key-round rests on the crafter's recomputation of the pinned lucide-static 1.75.0 tarball hash, which I cannot re-verify here (no tarball in the tree, and I install nothing); check-arch verifies vendored-file hashes, not an upstream tarball. Import metadata was not supplied with this packet, so exercised changed targets are unmeasured; I treat that as unmeasured, not as a pass or a failure.

diagnostic: Accepted with four non-blocking findings. The candidate delivers the Request's move: three unconditional anchors to /teams, /workspace/invites and /admin/tokens sit after Board inside nav#sidebar-nav in the one partial that owns the member list, each with exactly one inline glyph and one word and no second name channel, and Home's Quick actions section is gone with its greeting, workspace line and Your projects intact; DashboardRoot drops the three fields that lost their only reader, so the nav is the page's single carrier of those facts and a reintroduced link cannot read them. The Request's second half, a collapsible left nav, is recorded in the authority brief as delivered in v0.19.0, and P4 keeps the folded-rail obligation for the three new members. Oracle completeness against the Request: P1, P2 and P3 each have an executable stimulus over real HTTP and falsifying assertions - ordered word/href equality over the closed four-member rights domain plus the no-project fallback, per-member shape with a non-vacuity guard, and the landing page's absence assertions paired with three positive readings; P4's shape half is falsified for every present and future member by the new enumerating check-arch layer. Every changed test path lies inside the recorded oracle or its declared supports, and each change is necessitated: the owed set in the icon-rail lane is widened, not relaxed; the six .actions palette rows are removed because their selector no longer exists on any served page, with the rail and nav palette still covered by three surviving quantified theme scenarios; the two eip-06 rows pinned the dashboard BODY as the offering surface and are superseded, with the page-wide leak falsifier for non-admins intact; the two xtask in-file edits are existing gate DATA its fail-closed shape requires. No testing-theater pattern, no mock, no softened fixture and no narrowed input. Evidence: host-owned cargo xtask smoke all gates green, whose inputs are byte-identical at this commit, carrying check-arch, the foundry-app and xtask tests, fmt and clippy; host-owned default acceptance lane 1912 scenarios, 1912 passed, in which I verified the slice oracle's ten scenarios green. Limits I keep explicit: the two @needs-browser lanes are observed only in the producer's craft record because the host lane excludes Docker and my own queued run of them could not start behind the shared VM lock (R6, and the P4 finding), so P4's runtime half and the renamed theme scenario are not independently observed - mechanically, the renamed step text is byte-identical on both sides and the collapsed and 480 px rules are member-quantified with the stylesheet untouched; icon provenance against the upstream tarball is not re-verifiable here; import metadata was not supplied, so exercised changed targets are unmeasured; typesafe: unavailable (jev_decide.py exit 3, TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent), so every reason here is a reviewer_reason checked against the cited bytes. Findings, none blocking and each with an owner: the empty CHANGELOG Unreleased section against this repository's own craft-time precedent (implementation); a duplicate attribute-reading helper beside the existing tag_attribute owner in check_arch.rs (implementation); a dead 'the dashboard' alternative in the eip-06 follows-step regex that no scenario drives any more (oracle); and the unobserved browser-lane evidence for P4 (implementation).
